punchline: Where you put your thumbs may say more about your confidence than your opening sentence does.
thirty_sec: Joe Navarro, a former FBI agent, noticed how much people read from posture before anyone speaks. Confident people tend to claim space: hands on hips, fingertips steepled. Unsure people shrink, pulling their arms in and hiding their hands or thumbs. He isn't selling a pose that rewires your hormones. His point is simpler. Your body is already telling the room how sure you feel, so it's worth knowing what it says.
question: Who do you know who looks confident before they say a word, and what are they actually doing?
